module_title: Acid Rain, Water Pollution, and Bio-Indicators
introduction: At this level, we understand how air pollution turns rain into acid, and how we scientifically measure the invisible levels of organic pollution in lakes and rivers.

core_concepts.title: Acid Rain
core_concepts.description:
Rainwater is considered acidic when its pH drops 'below 5.6'. 
Cause: Sulfur Dioxide ($SO_2$) and Nitrogen Oxides ($NO_x$) emitted from factories and vehicles react with water vapor in the atmosphere to form 'Sulfuric Acid' ($H_2SO_4$) and 'Nitric Acid' ($HNO_3$), respectively.

core_concepts.title: Stone Leprosy (Yellowing of the Taj Mahal)
core_concepts.description: When acid rain falls on marble (Calcium Carbonate - $CaCO_3$), it corrodes it. The yellowing and degradation of the 'Taj Mahal' due to $SO_2$ emissions from the nearby Mathura Oil Refinery is the most famous example of this phenomenon.

core_concepts.title: BOD (Biochemical Oxygen Demand)
core_concepts.description:
The most important metric for measuring water pollution. 
It is the amount of dissolved oxygen needed by aerobic biological organisms (bacteria) to break down organic waste in a water sample. 
Rule of Thumb: **The HIGHER the BOD, the MORE polluted the water is** (because bacteria are consuming all the oxygen, leaving none for fish).

core_concepts.title: Eutrophication and Biomagnification
core_concepts.description:
1. Eutrophication: The nutrient enrichment of lakes (due to agricultural fertilizer runoff containing Nitrates and Phosphates) causing massive 'Algal Blooms' that deplete oxygen. 
2. Biomagnification: The increasing concentration of toxic, non-biodegradable chemicals (like DDT and Mercury) at each successive level of the food chain (e.g., Plankton $\rightarrow$ Small Fish $\rightarrow$ Large Fish $\rightarrow$ Birds).

important_entities.name: Lichens
important_entities.significance: Lichens (a symbiotic relationship between fungi and algae) are extremely sensitive to air pollution, particularly 'Sulfur Dioxide ($SO_2$)'. They will not grow in polluted areas. Hence, they are used as excellent natural bio-indicators of air quality.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Examiners will try to confuse you with options like 'Biological Oxygen Demand' vs. 'Biochemical Oxygen Demand'. Always remember, the correct, exact scientific term is **Biochemical Oxygen Demand**.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: S ($SO_2$) makes Sulfuric acid. N ($NO_x$) makes Nitric acid. A = Acid Rain.

exam_strategy_tips: A highly repeated UPSC/Banking question: 'If the BOD of a river is very high, what does it indicate?' Answer: It indicates that the river is 'highly polluted' with organic matter.
